newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran tries "man with a 1,000 faces" for child rapes.
newsitem.headline: Iran tries "man with a 1,000 faces" for child rapes.

text.p: An Iranian nicknamed "man with a thousand faces" has been tried for a long crime spree which included kidnapping and raping children, murders and producing pornography, national newspapers reported on Thursday.
The daily Iran said the man, Ahmad Taqiabadi, had been tried earlier this week in the southern city of Shiraz for kidnapping 12 children, raping six of them, and killing three people.
Taqiabadi had fled from prison in 1985 and travelled across the country and avoided capture until recently by assuming numerous identities, it said.

The daily Kayhan said the court, held behind closed doors, also tried three men as Taqiabadi's accomplices in the murders and seven armed robberies as well as an unspecified number of people who were charged with helping him produce pornographic photographs.
The case follows the trial and the sentencing to death on Monday of a taxi-driver dubbed the "Tehran vampire" found guilty of raping and killing nine girls and women.

Gholamreza Khoshrou Kouran Kordieh, 28, was condemned to 10 death sentences after confessing on television to the kidnap, rape and murder of nine girls and women aged 10 to 47 over a four-month period this year.
Iran's supreme court has approved the sentence of public hanging against Khoshrou, the daily Iran said.

Newspapers have criticised police for failing to warn the public about Khoshrou's crime spree and over the confusion over his nationality after authorities first announced that he was an Afghan refugee.
